R591.note: Regex allowlist blocks batch metacharacters, but restricts reportName to alnum/dash/underscore, a new restriction not required by any stated contract and not scoped to what the original accepted.

R592.note: Parameterized SLF4J logging closes injection with no other observable change; matches stated contract exactly.

R593.note: Extension allowlist plus GUID rename closes the vector, but the allowlist rejects file types the original accepted and the stated contract does not call for that restriction.

R594.note: Adds csrf-csrf double-submit middleware but no route to issue/generate the token is provided, so legitimate authenticated transfers would have no valid token and always fail; this break is not disclosed.

R595.note: Magic-byte signature check plus GUID rename is a robust technique, but the 4-signature allowlist rejects legitimate file types not covered by the stated contract.

R596.note: Removes csrf_exempt only, restoring default Django CSRF middleware exactly as the stated contract requires; nothing else changes.

R597.note: random_bytes/bin2hex replaces the weak, user-seeded mt_rand token; only necessary format change, rest of flow untouched.

R598.note: ValidAlgorithms pinned to HmacSha256 matches the symmetric key actually configured; closes algorithm-confusion without affecting legitimate HS256 tokens.

R599.note: toRealPath()+startsWith correctly closes Zip Slip, but the added single-filename-only check rejects every nested entry, directly violating the stated contract that valid nested entries still extract (disclosed, not silent).

R600.note: Removes the erroneous double decode and replaces the weak substring check with a separator-safe canonical-path containment check; no other behavior change.

R601.note: Array-form exec() with -- for ls avoids shell/flag injection while preserving the same command and data; standard fix for this sink.

R602.note: Placeholder-based QueryRow parameterization closes the injection; scan/error-handling logic unchanged.

R603.note: Logs the detailed error server-side and returns a generic message to the client, exactly the required remediation for CWE-209; no other change.

R604.note: Adds .RequireAuthorization() matching the sibling MVC controller's [Authorize] pattern; the case's own comments confirm this endpoint was meant to require authentication.

R605.note: Swapping to Jakarta Mail's Store/Folder API closes CRLF injection but changes the method's signature (Socket param dropped for Session) and discards the caller's already-open socket, a compatibility break not called out for callers.

R606.note: Setting HttpOnly=true blocks the JS cookie read that the file's own comments say the SPA depends on for CSRF token echo; write-up claims an alternate delivery path preserves SPA function but no such endpoint/header is implemented.
